irrigated_growth_bonus_pct.note: percent reduction to a crop's days-to-mature while it is actively irrigated by this item (needs is_connected water). A property of the IRRIGATION ITEM, not the crop, so every crop reads the same value from the item watering it. Set on water_sprinkler, water_irrigation_sprinkler_riser and water_hose_soaker_flat; omit/0 elsewhere. Replaces the old per-crop irrigated_growth_bonus_pct.

power_draw_w.note: watts drawn while running, for electric pumps only. 0 for passive plumbing/storage items AND for manual/human-powered pumps - the pending Hand Pump Well Head is a real pump with real max_flow_rate_lpm but draws no electricity (arm-powered), so it's the one pump-type item that stays 0 here.

capacity_l.note: liters this item can store/hold. 0 for pumps, pipes/fittings/hoses, filters, and other non-storage items. Storage is passive/inert on its own - a barrel/cistern/tote/tank can't send water anywhere without a pump attached (see max_flow_rate_lpm); it just holds it until something pumps it out.

max_flow_rate_lpm.note: PRODUCER side - liters per in-game minute a pump can draw from its source (well/cistern) and push into the system. 0 for everything that isn't a pump. This includes the pending manual Hand Pump Well Head - it's not electric (power_draw_w stays 0) but it's a real pump with a real (lower, human-powered) throughput here; only the pending Manual Well (bucket-and-rope) has no flow rate at all, since it's a one-bucket-at-a-time manual draw rather than a continuous pump. RAIN BARRELS ARE ALSO PRODUCERS BUT DELIBERATELY GET 0 HERE, NOT A STATIC VALUE: a rain barrel's actual input rate is dynamic, not a fixed mechanical rating like a pump - it must be computed at runtime as roof_area_m2 (from whichever structure it's placed next to, see structures.schema.json) x current rain intensity x a runoff-efficiency constant. Do not backfill a fake constant flow rate for rain barrels here; the field structurally can't represent that and stays 0.

water_usage_lpm.note: CONSUMER side - liters per in-game minute drawn while actively running (sprinklers, hoses, watering wand). 0 for producers, storage, and passive/inline components. Fill-and-carry containers (bucket, jug, watering can) use capacity_l instead, not a flow rate. IRRIGATION ITEMS ARE TERMINAL: water_sprinkler, water_irrigation_sprinkler_riser, and water_hose_soaker_flat need water pumped TO them (is_connected still applies) but don't feed water onward to any other item - their output is a crop GROWTH-RATE MODIFIER for nearby farming category items, not more plumbing. Implemented as irrigated_growth_bonus_pct on these irrigation items themselves (the fertilizer equivalent is fertilizer_growth_bonus_pct on the fertilizer items).

is_connected.note: Same cascading model as internet.is_connected - default baseline, not a fixed fact. Pumps are producers and default true (they draw from a well/ground source, the origin). Fixed storage that's piped into the system (cistern, IBC tote, pressure tank) defaults false until wired to a producer. The rain barrel defaults true as its BASELINE type-level state, but a placed instance's actual connectivity also depends on max_roof_proximity_m being satisfied - see that field. Consumer fixtures (sprinklers, hoses, wand) default false until connected. Portable/hand-filled containers (bucket, jug, watering can) and passive inline components (pipe, fittings, filters, hose reels) stay false - they're not part of the piped network's connectivity graph.

max_filter_throughput_lpm.note: WATER CONTAMINATION mechanic: raw water drawn from a producer (well pump, manual well, hand pump) may be contaminated and must pass through a filter to become safe/clean before reaching consumer fixtures. This is the max liters per in-game minute a filter can clean at once - if demand from downstream consumers exceeds this rate, water only gets cleaned up to the filter's throughput and the excess is a bottleneck (unfiltered/contaminated water gets through, or supply is capped - exact behavior is a game-logic decision, not defined here). Filter items only. 0 for everything else in this category.

max_roof_proximity_m.note: PLACEMENT CONSTRAINT for rain barrels only: the barrel only actually collects water (counts as a working producer) if placed within this many meters of a structure's roofline - a rain barrel sitting out in the open with no nearby roof catches nothing. Game logic should check this distance at placement/runtime against the nearest structure before treating the barrel as is_connected/producing. 0 for every other item (not a spatial constraint for pumps, wells, storage, or fixtures).
